# Clearbot
Autonomous electric boats that collect floating waste

Spun out of University of Hong Kong students; builds self-driving electric boats that each collect 250-300 kg of waste per trip. Reported deployments in Hong Kong, India and Panama.

Sector: Ocean cleanup
Location: Hong Kong
Stage: seed

## Readiness (KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence)
- Customer (CRL) 6: Customer testing confirms value; structured sales activities started.
- Technology (TRL) 7: Near-complete prototype works in an operational environment.
- Business model (BRL) 5: Revenue and cost sides validated with external feedback; P&L updated.
- IP (IPRL) 4: Protectability confirmed by professional; priorities decided.
- Team (TMRL) 5: Founding team with main competencies; shareholder agreement signed.
- Funding (FRL) 5: Investor pitch tested; 12-month budget; funding strategy decided.
Robots deployed in several countries; seed-stage company, round size undisclosed.

## Ocean impact
- A clean ocean, Volume of macro-plastic diverted from nature (or landfill) (B2): Each robot collects 250-300 kg of floating waste per trip. (qualitative evidence)
- Positive socio-economic outcomes, Number of jobs created (F1): Deployments create local operator jobs (claimed). (claimed)

## Funding
- seed: undisclosed amount (2022-09), led by Alibaba Hong Kong Entrepreneurs Fund. Amount undisclosed. Co-investors: Earth Venture Capital, Asia Sustainability Angels, CarbonX Capital.

## Sources
- HiveLife: Clearbot

# Kelp Blue
Giant kelp forests for carbon, biodiversity and biostimulants

Dutch-headquartered company cultivating giant kelp forests off Lüderitz, Namibia. Received the Zayed Sustainability Prize (Climate Action) at COP28.

Sector: Aquaculture
Location: Lüderitz, Namibia
Stage: project-finance
Founded: 2020
Website: https://kelp.blue

## Readiness (KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence)
- Customer (CRL) 5: Customers confirm the product can solve their problem (problem-solution fit).
- Technology (TRL) 6: Representative prototype demonstrated in a relevant environment.
- Business model (BRL) 5: Revenue and cost sides validated with external feedback; P&L updated.
- IP (IPRL) 3: Key IP described in detail; initial protectability evaluation.
- Team (TMRL) 7: Well-functioning team with clear roles; board and advisors operational.
- Funding (FRL) 6: Improved pitch tested; 3-5 year P&L and cash flow.
Large-scale pilot forest in Namibia; project finance committed in principle but not yet confirmed as drawn.

## Ocean impact
- Sustainably managed ocean resources, Volume of biomass preserved or restored (A1): Kelp forest habitat increases local biomass (claimed). (claimed)
- Thriving and restored marine habitats, Area of kelp forest protected or restored (C5): Cultivates giant kelp forests off Lüderitz, Namibia. (qualitative evidence)
- Towards 1.5C, Carbon sequestered (D3): Carbon capture from kelp forests (claimed). (claimed)
- Positive socio-economic outcomes, Number of jobs created (F1): Creates local jobs in Lüderitz (claimed). (claimed)

## Funding
- project-finance: 60,000,000 USD (2023-12), led by Climate Fund Managers; Eos Capital. In-principle commitment, released in phases, pending investment and Namibian regulatory approvals. A separate ~$80M blue bond was planned on the NSX.

## Sources
- The Fish Site: Kelp Blue seeks $80M blue bond
- The Brief: Kelp Blue blue bonds

# Notpla
Seaweed-based packaging that replaces single-use plastic

Develops packaging and coatings made from seaweed and plants as an alternative to single-use plastic.

Sector: Materials & packaging
Location: London, United Kingdom
Stage: series-a
Founded: 2014
Website: https://www.notpla.com

## Readiness (KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence)
- Customer (CRL) 8: Market-ready product sold near target price; initial traction; sales process staffed.
- Technology (TRL) 8: Complete technology proven in actual operations by first users.
- Business model (BRL) 7: First commercial revenue shows willingness to pay; key partner agreements in place.
- IP (IPRL) 6: Complete IP strategy; positive response from authorities; freedom-to-operate assessed.
- Team (TMRL) 7: Well-functioning team with clear roles; board and advisors operational.
- Funding (FRL) 8: Term-sheet-level discussions; due-diligence materials ready.
Products on the market and a large Series A+ imply commercial traction; IP position not verified.

## Ocean impact
- A clean ocean, Volume of macro-plastic diverted from nature (or landfill) (B2): Seaweed-based packaging replaces single-use plastic items. (qualitative evidence)
- Towards 1.5C, GHG emissions reduced or avoided (D1): Lower-carbon materials than fossil plastics (claimed). (claimed)

## Funding
- series-a: 20,000,000 GBP (2024-09), led by UB Forest Industry Green Growth Fund. Series A+ (~EUR 23M).

## Sources
- EU Maritime Forum: Notpla £20M Series A+

# Ocean Rainforest
Offshore seaweed cultivation at scale

Cultivates seaweed offshore in the Faroe Islands and develops seaweed products and markets.

Sector: Aquaculture
Location: Faroe Islands
Stage: series-a
Website: https://www.oceanrainforest.com

## Readiness (KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence)
- Customer (CRL) 6: Customer testing confirms value; structured sales activities started.
- Technology (TRL) 7: Near-complete prototype works in an operational environment.
- Business model (BRL) 6: Complete sustainable business model tested in realistic scenarios (pilot, pre-order).
- IP (IPRL) 4: Protectability confirmed by professional; priorities decided.
- Team (TMRL) 7: Well-functioning team with clear roles; board and advisors operational.
- Funding (FRL) 7: Discussions with investors around a defined offer; business plan in place.
Operating offshore farms in the Faroes; Series A to scale production and markets.

## Ocean impact
- Sustainably managed ocean resources, Tonnes of ocean-based seaweed and bivalves produced (A4): Produces offshore-farmed seaweed in the Faroe Islands. (qualitative evidence)
- Towards 1.5C, Carbon sequestered (D3): Seaweed cultivation as a carbon sink (claimed). (claimed)
- Climate-resilient coastal communities, Enhanced food security (E4): Seaweed as a food and feed resource. (claimed)

## Funding
- series-a: 6,200,000 USD (2023-02), led by The Grantham Foundation. With Katapult Ocean (Deep Blue fund), Builders Vision, Ocean Born Foundation, WWF-US.

## Sources
- Undercurrent News: Ocean Rainforest $6.2M Series A

# Oceanium
Seaweed biorefinery for food, materials and biodegradable products

Processes farmed kelp into food ingredients, biodegradable materials and other products through its biorefinery technology.

Sector: Aquaculture
Location: Oban, United Kingdom
Stage: seed
Website: https://www.oceanium.world

## Readiness (KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence)
- Customer (CRL) 5: Customers confirm the product can solve their problem (problem-solution fit).
- Technology (TRL) 6: Representative prototype demonstrated in a relevant environment.
- Business model (BRL) 5: Revenue and cost sides validated with external feedback; P&L updated.
- IP (IPRL) 5: Draft IP strategy; first formal application of key IP filed.
- Team (TMRL) 6: Complementary, diverse founding team with clear CEO; advisors being recruited.
- Funding (FRL) 5: Investor pitch tested; 12-month budget; funding strategy decided.
Biorefinery tech scaling ahead of a planned Series A for a commercial plant.

## Ocean impact
- Sustainably managed ocean resources, Tonnes of ocean-based seaweed and bivalves produced (A4): Creates demand for farmed kelp. (claimed)
- A clean ocean, Volume of macro-plastic diverted from nature (or landfill) (B2): Biodegradable materials as plastic alternatives. (claimed)

## Funding
- seed: 2,600,000 USD (2023-09), led by Builders Vision. Pre-Series A raise to commercialise; WWF and Green Angel Ventures participated.
- seed: 2,000,000 GBP, led by Green Angel Syndicate. Seed II first close; WWF anchor; Katapult Ocean, Sky Ocean Ventures, Scottish Enterprise previously invested.

## Sources
- FoodNavigator: Oceanium secures fresh funds
- SeafoodSource: Oceanium £2M

# Seabound
Onboard carbon capture for ships

Builds carbon capture equipment that fits on ships to capture exhaust CO2 at the source. Y Combinator alumnus.

Sector: Shipping decarbonisation
Location: London, United Kingdom
Stage: seed
Founded: 2021
Website: https://www.seabound.co

## Readiness (KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence)
- Customer (CRL) 6: Customer testing confirms value; structured sales activities started.
- Technology (TRL) 6: Representative prototype demonstrated in a relevant environment.
- Business model (BRL) 5: Revenue and cost sides validated with external feedback; P&L updated.
- IP (IPRL) 5: Draft IP strategy; first formal application of key IP filed.
- Team (TMRL) 6: Complementary, diverse founding team with clear CEO; advisors being recruited.
- Funding (FRL) 6: Improved pitch tested; 3-5 year P&L and cash flow.
Seed-stage hardware moving through ship pilots, with government grant support.

## Ocean impact
- Towards 1.5C, GHG emissions reduced or avoided (D1): Captures CO2 from ship exhaust onboard. (qualitative evidence)
- Towards 1.5C, SOx emissions mitigated (D5): Co-capture of sulphur emissions (claimed). (claimed)

## Funding
- grant: 1,100,000 GBP (2025), led by UK Clean Maritime Demonstration Competition (Round 6). Reported by aggregators; verify against the UK DfT announcement.
- seed: 4,400,000 USD (2022-05), led by Lowercarbon Capital. With Eastern Pacific Shipping, Emles, Hawktail, Rebel Fund, Soma Capital, Y Combinator.

## Sources
- TechCrunch: Seabound carbon capture for container ships
- TNW: UK startup Seabound

# SeaForester
Restoring marine forests

Marine restoration company focused on restoring kelp and other marine forests.

Sector: Habitat restoration
Location: Lisbon, Portugal
Stage: seed

## Readiness (KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence)
- Customer (CRL) 4: Problem confirmed by multiple customers; segments and buyer roles identified.
- Technology (TRL) 5: Components validated in a relevant (simulated) environment.
- Business model (BRL) 4: Simplified P&L indicates viability; initial sustainability assessment (own assumptions).
- IP (IPRL) 3: Key IP described in detail; initial protectability evaluation.
- Team (TMRL) 5: Founding team with main competencies; shareholder agreement signed.
- Funding (FRL) 5: Investor pitch tested; 12-month budget; funding strategy decided.
Fresh seed round; restoration business model still being validated.

## Ocean impact
- Sustainably managed ocean resources, Volume of biomass preserved or restored (A1): Restored forests increase marine biomass (claimed). (claimed)
- Thriving and restored marine habitats, Area of kelp forest protected or restored (C5): Restores kelp / marine forests. (qualitative evidence)
- Towards 1.5C, Carbon sequestered (D3): Blue-carbon sequestration (claimed). (claimed)

## Funding
- seed: 1,900,000 USD (2025-10), led by WWF; Schmidt Marine Technology Partners. Co-led.

## Sources
- Seedtable: SeaForester seed 2025-10

# Sofar Ocean
Real-time ocean data from a global network of Spotter buoys

Builds solar-powered Spotter buoys that report wind, wave, temperature and current data, and sells marine weather intelligence. Formed from the merger of OpenROV and Spoondrift.

Sector: Ocean data
Location: San Francisco, United States
Stage: series-b
Founded: 2019
Website: https://www.sofarocean.com

## Readiness (KTH Innovation Readiness Level 1-9, assessed 2026-10-16, low confidence)
- Customer (CRL) 8: Market-ready product sold near target price; initial traction; sales process staffed.
- Technology (TRL) 9: Scalable technology proven in operations by several users over time.
- Business model (BRL) 7: First commercial revenue shows willingness to pay; key partner agreements in place.
- IP (IPRL) 6: Complete IP strategy; positive response from authorities; freedom-to-operate assessed.
- Team (TMRL) 8: Experienced leadership team; competent board; HR processes in place.
- Funding (FRL) 8: Term-sheet-level discussions; due-diligence materials ready.
Thousands of buoys deployed across all major oceans; Series B-backed team.

## Ocean impact
- Towards 1.5C, GHG emissions reduced or avoided (D1): Weather routing can reduce ship fuel use (claimed). (claimed)
- Climate-resilient coastal communities, Use of ocean information products/services in climate adaptation decisions (E2): Real-time wind, wave, temperature and current data used in marine decisions. (qualitative evidence)

## Funding
- series-b: 39,000,000 USD (2021-11), led by Union Square Ventures; Foundry Group. Aggregators list total raised between ~$47M and ~$73M; unverified.

## Sources
- TechCrunch: Sofar nets $39M Series B

# Origin by Ocean
Website: https://www.originbyocean.com/

## Identity and registry
Name: Origin by Ocean Oy
Aliases: Nauvu, Ocean Orchard Oy
Website domain: originbyocean.com
Business id: 2982879-2
Country: Finland
City: Espoo
Legal form: limited company
Founded date: 2019-03-01
Status: active
Industry code: 20590

## Blue-economy profile
Blue sector: blue biotechnology
Ocean problem: The company addresses the environmental crisis caused by invasive algae blooms and ocean pollution by transforming these challenges into regenerative solutions.
Solution summary: The company turns invasive Sargassum into functional, bio-based ingredients for industries like cosmetics, food, and textiles through a unique biorefining process.
Customer type: B2B
Target customers: consumer goods, food and feed industry, chemicals and materials

## Technology
Tech description: Our biorefinery platform separates invasive algae into multiple valuable ingredients, each with its own function and commercial application.
Dev stage: commercial operation

## Business

Business model: product sale
Customer validation: paying customers
Paying customers: names: Ole Hyvä Luonnontuote, Marimekko, sauna/ing, No Niin Cosmetics

## Ocean impact
Impact claim: Invasive Sargassum blooms place pressure on coastal ecosystems and communities, and we use this biomass as a raw material for ingredients to restore marine ecosystems.
Impact pathway: Invasive Sargassum blooms place pressure on coastal ecosystems; by removing harmful algae and using it in a circular biorefinery to produce bio-based ingredients, we restore marine ecosystems while building scalable value chains.

# ReelData AI
Website: http://www.reeldata.ai/

## Identity and registry
Name: ReelData AI
Website domain: reeldata.ai
Country: Canada
City: Dartmouth

## Blue-economy profile
Blue sector: aquaculture
Ocean problem: Aquaculture operations face high feed waste, elevated fish mortality, and environmental impacts from a lack of precise operational data.
Solution summary: ReelData provides an AI and computer vision suite that delivers automated feeding, biomass monitoring, and health tracking for land-based fish farms.
Customer type: B2B
Target customers: fish farms

## Technology
Tech description: ReelData uses AI and camera monitoring in land-based aquaculture to track fish behavior and biomass and autonomously adjust feeding based on real-time appetite.
Dev stage: commercial operation
- Pilots: partner: Fifax

## Business
Value proposition: ReelData provides land-based aquaculture farms with data and automation to maximize growth, minimize costs, and reduce risk.
Customer validation: unpaid pilot

## Ocean impact
Impact claim: ReelData claims its AI suite enables aquaculture farms to operate with greater sustainability and minimize their environmental impact.
Impact pathway: By automatically detecting real-time fish appetite and adjusting feed levels accordingly, the platform prevents overfeeding and limits aquaculture waste.

## Funding and deal
- Equity rounds: stage: series a; amount: 8,000,000; currency: USD
Total raised: 7,440,000
Stage: series a

## Marketing and distribution
Sales channels: partners
Distribution partners: Farm in a Box
